{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary objective omits key secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The secondary objectives for both Group 1 and Group 2 are to: investigator review, and overall survival (OS)",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The secondary objectives sentence is incomplete, listing only 'investigator review' and OS, but omitting other endpoints like duration of response, PFS, and CR rate that are listed in Section 4.2.2. This inconsistency may cause confusion about the study's objectives.",
      "fix": "Complete the sentence to include all secondary endpoints (e.g., 'to assess duration of response, progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and other endpoints as specified in Section 4.2.2')."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for HHI intolerance is overly complex and restrictive",
      "quote": "Or any of the following HHI-related events in patients with at least 3 months of exposure to HHI therapy (exclusive of treatment breaks): Grade 2 muscle spasms or myalgias (iia) Grade 2 dysgeusia or anorexia, if accompanied by ≥Grade 1 weight loss (iib) Grade 2 nausea or diarrhea despite medical management or (iic)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The criteria for intolerance are very specific and may exclude patients who have significant but different Grade 2 toxicities (e.g., fatigue, rash) that are not listed. This could limit enrollment and lead to amendments to broaden criteria.",
      "fix": "Consider broadening intolerance criteria to include any Grade 2 toxicity that persists despite optimal management, or allow medical monitor discretion for other Grade 2 events."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for 'no better than stable disease after 9 months' is ambiguous",
      "quote": "No better than a stable disease after 9 months on HHI therapy (exclusive of treatment breaks)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'no better than a stable disease' is ambiguous—does it include patients with partial response that later progresses? It also requires a specific duration of therapy, which may be difficult to verify and could lead to enrollment delays or amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether this applies only to patients with stable disease as best response, and specify how to document the 9-month period (e.g., from start of HHI therapy)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for measurable disease in Group 2 is restrictive for non-photography lesions",
      "quote": "Group 2: At baseline, there must be at least 1 measurable baseline lesion in which the longest diameter and the perpendicular diameter are both ≥10 mm if measured by digital medical photography.",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This criterion requires bi-dimensional measurements ≥10 mm for lesions measured by photography, but for lesions measured by MRI/CT (as allowed later in the same section), only RECIST 1.1 criteria (≥10 mm in longest dimension) are required. This inconsistency may exclude patients with lesions that are measurable by RECIST but not by photography, and could be burdensome for sites.",
      "fix": "Harmonize the measurement criteria for Group 2 lesions, e.g., allow RECIST 1.1 for all imaging modalities and specify photography for external lesions only."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for hepatic function is overly permissive and inconsistent",
      "quote": "Total bilirubin ≤3.0x upper limit of normal (ULN) (or ≤3x ULN, if liver metastases). Patients with Gilbert’s Disease and total bilirubin up to 3x ULN may be eligible after communication with and approval from the medical monitor",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Allowing total bilirubin up to 3x ULN (even without liver metastases) is unusually high for an immunotherapy trial and may increase risk of hepatotoxicity. Also, the note for hepatic metastases in Group 1 is complex and may be difficult to implement.",
      "fix": "Consider standard limits (e.g., ≤1.5x ULN) unless liver metastases are present, and simplify the hepatic metastasis criteria."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for CPK elevation is vague",
      "quote": "Creatine phosphokinase (CPK) (also known as CK [creatine kinase]) elevation ≤ grade 2",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The criterion does not specify a baseline value or how to grade CPK elevation (e.g., per CTCAE). This could lead to variability in interpretation and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Specify the grading system (e.g., CTCAE v4.0) and clarify whether this is based on local lab normal ranges."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for prior radiation is complex and may delay enrollment",
      "quote": "A clinic note from the investigator indicating that an individualized benefit:risk assessment was performed by a multidisciplinary team (consisting of, at minimum, a radiation oncologist AND EITHER a medical oncologist with expertise in cutaneous malignancies OR a dermato-oncologist, OR a head and neck surgeon) within 60 days prior to enrollment",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring a multidisciplinary team assessment for patients who have not received prior radiation is burdensome and may be difficult to arrange in a timely manner, potentially delaying enrollment and causing amendments.",
      "fix": "Simplify the requirement, e.g., allow a single radiation oncologist's assessment, or remove the multidisciplinary team requirement for patients with clear contraindications."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for prior malignancy is overly broad",
      "quote": "Ongoing or recent (within 5 years) evidenc",
      "page": 42,
      "section": "6.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The exclusion criterion is cut off mid-sentence, making it incomplete and uninterpretable. This is a critical issue as it leaves a major eligibility criterion undefined.",
      "fix": "Complete the sentence, e.g., 'Ongoing or recent (within 5 years) evidence of significant concurrent malignancy, except for non-melanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.'"
    }
  ]
}
